In school, you're taught what skills do you need to be a great leader? Leadership. Leadership skills. But what are they? Responsibility, right? Wisdom. Openness. Empathy. Respect. Knowledge. This is what you're taught in school. And we can go on for a long time. Okay. There are hundreds of skills you need to be a great leader. Guess what guys? Wrong. To be a great leader in the world and history, you need three skills. Analyze what the leaders of today are like, Putin, Trump, every leader in the world shares these three skills.

The first is unpredictability. People cannot predict how you will behave; you are a mystery to people. The second skill is high stress tolerance. Donald Trump is probably the most hated man in America. Guess what guys? He goes to bed and sleeps like a baby. He does not care. He gets up, tweets, gives speeches, talks to reporters, and is the happiest man alive. And so, the last skill is lack of empathy. He cares only about himself.

All you need are these three skills to do well in life: unpredictability, no one knows how you think or behave; high stress tolerance, you don't care; lack of empathy, you're very selfish. These are the three skills leaders need to succeed. But we can just use one word to describe all three: dissociation. Dissociation means your mind is part of your body. When you dissociate, your mind leaves your body so that you don't think what's happening is happening to you; it's happening to someone else. You become an observer in a movie.

Another term for dissociation is multiple personality disorder. Donald Trump is unpredictable because he's literally 100 different people in different circumstances. That's why you can never predict how he will behave. Great leaders in history were like that. Game theory explains this. In games with millions of players, the secret to winning is cheating through forming secret alliances. To win, you must be part of many powerful groups. However, secret societies make you loyal and obedient by creating multiple personalities. Spies are recruited based on their ability to dissociate, lack empathy.

In real life, a person with the most multiple personalities wins. But when we go back to ancient Egypt, pharaohs are born into that position. Can you create multiple personalities in a person? Yes. I'll show you how in Egypt. Remember, a pharaoh is born into that position.
